 Happening Wednesday: Mobile DMV, RCSD budget meeting, and Thanksgiving meal
 Evan Bourtis News10NBC 
 --> 
 ROCHESTER, N.Y. — Here’s your guide to what’s happening around the Rochester area on Wednesday. You can see more upcoming events in our  community calendar. 
 Ogden mobile DMV
 Monroe County’s mobile DMV is coming to Ogden Town Hall on Ogden Center Road on Wednesday. It runs from 10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. You’ll have access to a variety of services. However, permit testing, along with enhanced license and REAL ID transactions, aren’t available at mobile units.  You can learn about other upcoming mobile DMV units here .
 RCSD budget meeting
 The Rochester City School District wants the community’s input as it faces a projected $54 million budget gap for the next school year. RCSD is holding a forum on Wednesday where community members can ask questions and share feedback on the budget gap. It’s part of a series of hearings. Here’s the schedule:
 Wednesday, Nov. 18, 6:00 p.m. – Loretta Johnson Middle School Auditorium: An overview of the District’s financial outlook, budget challenges, and development process.
 Wednesday, Dec. 9, 6:00 p.m. – East High School: A discussion of community priorities, survey feedback, and emerging budget considerations.
 Thursday, Feb. 4, 2027, Virtual, 6:00 p.m. – An opportunity to review budget considerations and potential options as the District continues its planning.
 Thursday, March 11, 2027, Virtual, 6:00 p.m. – A discussion of the Superintendent’s proposed direction, community feedback, and next steps in the budget process.
 The district has also opened a community survey to get feedback. Families, students, and staff can weigh in on which programs and services matter most to them. You can take the survey online h e re now through Friday, Dec. 4. There will also be a separate survey sent to RCSD students in grades 7-12.
 The forums are open to all community members. Additional information about the virtual sessions will be shared closer to their scheduled dates. To learn more, click here. 
 Annual Rosa Wims Thanksgiving meal
 Foodlink is set to prepare hundreds of meals for people in need on Wednesday for its annual Rosa Wims Thanksgiving meal.
 It’s happening at St. Peter’s Kitchen on Brown Street from noon to 1:30 p.m. The meal honors the legacy of Rosa Wims, Rochester’s first Black nurse’s aide and a Foodlink board and staff member who won multiple awards for her service to the community. Her Thanksgiving meal tradition began in the mid-1970s on Jefferson Avenue with a few dozen guests and has grown to serve hundreds of people.
 Last year, Foodlink prepared more than 350 meals for the lunch crowd at St. Peter’s Kitchen and plans to make 450 this year. St. Peter’s Kitchen is considered the busiest meal program in Foodlink’s network, which includes hundreds of programs across 10 counties. There are other upcoming Thanksgiving meal programs across the region. See the full story here .
